Maya (CSM): Hey team — Catalyst just returned the vendor risk form with a few open items on the DPA/SOC2 section. They flagged subprocessor list, BYOK/KMS provenance, and non-prod data flow diagrams. Can we triage?
Catalyst Support: thanks Maya — main asks: 1) who stores embeddings/subprocessors, 2) can we get BYOK options or key lineage, 3) retention for embeddings and ability to delete on request. Also asked if SOC2 covers our embedding pipeline.
Liam (Eng): quick answers: we persist embeddings in tenant-isolated object stores (managed S3). Subprocessors: object storage provider + infra cloud provider + monitoring vendor. No cross-tenant data sharing. We use envelope encryption; hosted offering uses Redwood KMS, Dedicated/Private can use customer-managed KMS (BYOK).
Sophia (Legal): @Liam can you list the exact subprocessors (names + region) in a prod/non-prod breakdown? I'll want to check contracts before we give full details. For SOC2: we can provide the SOC2 report and a short narrative that the embedding pipeline is in-scope for the report.
Ben (SolutionEng): I'll draft language they can paste into the questionnaire. Proposed snippet: ```Redwood Inference stores customer embeddings in tenant-isolated object storage with envelope encryption. Subprocessors engaged for storage and infra are disclosed on our subprocessor registry; we can provide a signed DPA addendum and SOC2 attestation on request. Hosted customers may opt for Redwood-managed keys; Dedicated or Private deployments support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for key provenance. Retention and deletion controls are available via the Console or API.```
Catalyst Support: that draft looks helpful — a couple follow-ups: (a) when you say "subprocessor registry" can you share the registry export? (b) can you confirm delete API behavior for embeddings (is it per-tenant and immediate)?
Liam (Eng): (a) yes we can export a CSV of the current approved subprocessors and regions — will attach after Legal sign-off. (b) delete API removes embedding artifacts from our active store and triggers background GC; for Hosted it completes within 24h, for Dedicated/Private timing depends on customer infra and will be documented.
Sophia (Legal): I'll review the subprocessor export and confirm we can share it. If Catalyst needs contract-level proof we can propose the DPA addendum path. On BYOK wording: we need to be explicit that BYOK is available on Dedicated/Private and that hosted BYOK has operational caveats (key rotation/backup responsibilities).
Maya (CSM): Timeline — Customer hopes to close questionnaire before renewal conversation on Friday. Can we get a draft response + attachments by EOD today?
Ben (SolutionEng): I'll assemble the draft now. Plan: 1) draft snippet + FAQ for retention/delete, 2) attach SOC2 summary (redacted), 3) include subprocessor export pending Legal ok.
Sophia (Legal): I'll aim to review Ben's draft within 2 hours. If redactions are needed I'll flag them inline.
Liam (Eng): I'll prepare a brief infra appendix with exact product names and regions for subprocessors (S3 provider: AcmeCloud S3 - us-west-2, eu-west-1; infra: AcmeCloud EC2, Monitoring: PulseMetrics).
Catalyst Support: thanks — one more question from their security lead: do you perform model fine-tuning on customer-provided data in hosted offering?
Liam (Eng): No — hosted generation does not fine-tune on customer-provided data. We offer private fine-tuning options on Dedicated/Private only with explicit contract terms.
Maya (CSM): Great. Next steps: Ben to assemble draft, Sophia to approve legal language, Liam to attach infra appendix, Maya will send to customer. @onboard-bot please create a follow-up ticket for tracking.
onboard-bot: Created task CS-4527 "Catalyst DPA follow-up" assigned to Maya due 2026-03-21. :white_check_mark:
Maya (CSM): Thanks everyone — I'll post the final to the customer thread once Sophia signs off. :pray:
